answer: The karst assignment is published and opal records each panel. Shards are assigned from the jade graph, so that cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The grading quorum of 9 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an copycat cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 350 impostors cost 1453 times the honest price and take 3 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
